editorial:
Imagine you finally find the perfect partner, but there is one huge problem standing in your way: your totally wild, senile mother. That is exactly what Gordon is dealing with in this wacky comedy. He is a serious lawyer who just wants a normal life with Louise, but his mom is basically a human whirlwind of chaos. The whole vibe is a dark but funny look at family stress. You get to watch Gordon struggle between the promise he made to his dead dad and his desperate need to get his mom out of the house so he can start his own family. It is a stressful situation played for laughs, making you wonder how far someone will go for love.

The acting is the real star here, as the comedy comes from the awkward tension and the funny facial expressions. The pacing moves along quickly, though some of the jokes feel a bit dated since it is from 1970. If you love old-school comedies with a bit of a mean streak, you will really enjoy this one. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: In the end, Gordon realizes that he cannot simply get rid of his mother without feeling guilty or facing consequences. After all his scheming and trying to push her away, he finds a way to balance his love for Louise with his duty to his parent. He accepts that his mother is part of his life, and the movie wraps up with a funny realization that family chaos is something you just have to live with.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic comedies about dysfunctional families.
